newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police to serve summonses to balloon protesters.
newsitem.headline: HK police to serve summonses to balloon protesters.

text.p: Hong Kong police said on Wednesday they will serve summonses on demonstrators and journalists over a balloon protest in a restricted area near the Chinese border.
The demonstrators were protesting against Beijing's plan to replace the territory's legislature.
The 13 protesters and 17 journalists covering the story will receive the summonses for entering the closed frontier area without a permit, a police spokesman said.

The protest took place on December 21 when members of the United Front Against the Provisional Legislature drove into a restricted area at the Lok Ma Chau frontier post and launched 50 helium balloons carrying a banner opposing the interim council.
The provisional legislature was chosen that day in Shenzhen, just across the border in China, by a committee of 400 carefully chosen pro-China Hong Kong figures.
Police on Wednesday did not explain the delay in issuing the summonses.

China plans to install the new legislature next July 1 when it takes the colony back from Britain, and to disband the current Legislative Council that was elected by over one million Hong Kong voters in 1995.

"We cannot go into the Shenzhen area to protest but our balloons -- our spirit of protest -- will continue to fight against such an anti-democratic body," Andrew Cheng, a spokesman for the protestors, said at the time.
Cheng could not be reached for comment on Wednesday.
The head of the Hong Kong Journalists Association declined comment, but the association has said the reporters had not been warned and issuing summonses was inappropriate.
Nine of the 11 drivers of vehicles ferrying the protesters and journalists would also be called to appear, police said. They will appear in Fanling Court on April 30.
